newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin gives jobs, EU duties top budget priority.
newsitem.headline: Jospin gives jobs, EU duties top budget priority.

text.p: Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has told ministers to give "absolute priority" in the 1998 budget to fighting unemployment and injustice while respecting France's European Union commitments, his office said on Thursday.

Jospin's spokesman, Manuel Valls, told reporters that the instructions were contained in "framework letters" which the prime minister sends each year to ministers setting guidelines for preparing the budget.

Ministers must "include two essential elements, the absolute priority to the fight for employment and for social justice, while respecting our European commitments to achieve economic and monetary union (EMU) at the deadline foreseen by the (Maastricht) treaty," he said.
Valls said the letters did not contain any target figure for the 1998 budget deficit and the three percent of gross domestic product criterion in the treaty should be observed as a trend.

He also said that contrary to a report in the newspaper Le Monde, no decision had been taking yet on whether to go ahead with selling off a minority stake in France Telecom, as the previous centre-right government had planned to do.
